The central issue: outside full Action allowance can outlast the short owner slot/old End. Need lawful s+3 magical action on existing reinforcement/post-recovery/Ferry outside calendars, without erasing settled Ends, undoing decay, fictitious future turns or extra allowance. Preserve printed/source regular-End behavior in initiative unless an explicit justified source/policy decision resolves it. Investigate an outside activity accounting interval derived from actual owner Starts/allowance, with honest transition carry and no separate clock. Consider particularly real closure immediately after a tactical End has already settled, re-entry before next owner Start, partial intervals at mode/epoch changes, zero-Dissonance/no-End-row, long sparse advances and no gain/reset from repeated boundary switching. Do not approve a general drift from source merely for easier tests.

Address all six consumers and their downstream healing/Radiance/Aura/vent/recharge turn identities; no automatic new Action or source acquisition. Needed output: exact interval identity/open/close, eligibility for idle/Grounding reduction, attribution of late activity, ordering with conditions/effect expiry/recharge/work/pending choice, old-profile preservation, strict save/replay proof and genuine prospective witness routes. items.text:
**I recommend separating the identity of the spendable allowance from the interval eligible for Dissonance settlement.** They are currently treated too much like the same thing.

That lets an otherwise legal outside Action execute at `s+3`, preserves a tactical End already settled at `s+2`, and prevents closure or admission from creating another recovery opportunity.

This is a **concrete proposal for CAL-01–05**, not source/API acceptance. Your latest instruction lifts the owner’s implementation pause; the remaining prerequisite is actual agreement on the complete written contract before coding.

The governing sources are the pinned `CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md`, `COMBAT_ACTION_PLAYTEST.md` and `class_playtests/cleric.json`, alongside the [shared-world policy](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/cf02edf6154f79e6d3a7bc80f54dad4b122bde34/docs/unity/SHARED_WORLD_RULE_DECISIONS.md), [TAC-08 P3/P4](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/cf02edf6154f79e6d3a7bc80f54dad4b122bde34/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-15-tac08-cleric-casting/APPROVED_CASTING_CONTRACT.md), and [Consecration’s amended contract](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/cf02edf6154f79e6d3a7bc80f54dad4b122bde34/docs/unity/evidence/2026-11-17-chr05-consecration/SOURCE_API_CONTRACT.md). **The outside accounting and partial-interval rules below are proposed NEW integration policy, not quotations from those sources.**

1. **CAL-01 — One allowance identity, explicit activity segments, one settlement opportunity**

   Give each actor’s ordinary allowance a stable identity derived from the **actual event that supplied or refreshed it**:

   - Actor.
   - Originating epoch and actual processed owner Start.
   - For an initial carried allowance, its genuine admission/bootstrap provenance instead of an invented Start.

   Carry this identity across mode changes and epoch admission until an actual new owner Start refreshes the allowance. A new epoch ID, observation, save/load or control-mode change does not itself create a new allowance identity.

   Separately record activity segments belonging to that allowance:

   | Segment | Action admission | Dissonance accounting |
   |---|---|---|
   | Active initiative | Existing actual own-turn restrictions | Settle once at the actual regular End |
   | Ordinary outside interval | Any lawful time while the actual allowance remains available | Defer settlement through the outside accounting interval |
   | Remainder after settlement | Otherwise lawful outside Actions remain possible | No second idle/Grounding settlement |

   In an unchanged outside calendar, the accounting interval is `[s, s+6)`, derived from consecutive owner Starts. Its short virtual slot still ends at `s+2`; that marker continues to serve its existing consumers, but **does not settle outside Dissonance** in the successor profile.

   At `s+6`, settle the preceding interval before admitting voluntary actions using the refreshed allowance. An action exactly at that boundary belongs to the new allowance after required boundary processing.

   No client supplies these identities or chooses the segment classification. There is no new clock and no separate payment command.

2. **CAL-02 — Final settlements stay final; Grounding needs an available settlement opportunity**

   For an **unsettled** accounting interval, retain the existing exclusive outcomes:

   - Any qualifying spell or magical activity: no idle/Grounding reduction.
   - Otherwise, a genuine paid Grounding Action: reduce by PB.
   - Otherwise, a completed eligible idle interval: reduce by one.
   - Clamp at zero; never apply both reductions.

   Spell Dissonance, Refrain and the Cleric’s separately qualified paid vent retain their own rules. Passive concentration remains non-activity.

   For an interval whose **tactical End already settled**, later outside activity belongs to a new activity segment carrying the same allowance identity. It does not change the completed End’s flags or result, and it is not attributed to a future turn.

   **The nontrivial proposed eligibility decision:** Grounding is unavailable when that allowance has already consumed its idle/Grounding settlement opportunity. Reject before payment with a precise, filtered reason. Other otherwise lawful late Actions remain available.

   This restriction needs explicit concurrence in the amendment. It is not a claim that the printed source prohibits outside Grounding. It avoids three unacceptable alternatives: charging for a benefit that cannot settle, granting idle plus a second Grounding reduction, or reopening a completed End. Ordinary late Grounding remains supported when the outside interval is still unsettled.

   Zero Dissonance does not change eligibility. Record or deterministically prove that settlement occurred even when its numerical reduction was zero. **An omitted zero-effect End row cannot reopen an interval.**

   Illustrative timelines below use hypothetical starting Dissonance, not executed witnesses:

   | Situation | Required result |
   |---|---|
   | Already outside at `s`, Dissonance 5; Consecrate at `s+3` | No idle reduction at `s+2`; pay Action/2RP at `s+3`; settlement at `s+6` reduces nothing |
   | Already outside; Grounding at `s+3`, PB 2, Dissonance 5 | Pay Action once; settle to 3 at `s+6`, not 2 |
   | Already outside; no magical activity or Grounding | Dissonance 5→4 at `s+6` |
   | Tactical idle End settles 5→4 at `s+2`; genuine closure follows; Consecrate at `s+3` | Keep the completed 5→4 result; record the later paid activity separately; no second reduction at `s+6` |
   | Same completed-End remainder, but Grounding requested at `s+3` | Reject unchanged because its settlement opportunity is already consumed |

   A genuine paid Invocation in that remainder may still receive its independent protected vent if its actual expenditure and cadence qualify. “No second idle/Grounding settlement” must not suppress a different sourced effect.

3. **CAL-03 — Carry provenance and pending settlement, not fabricated turns**

   **Closure after an End:** finish the existing outgoing-slot procedure and preserve its consequences. Enter the remainder described above. Closure does not refresh allowance, cadence, recharge or settlement eligibility.

   **Closure before this actor’s own End:** if that actor’s settlement remains pending, carry its existing activity into outside accounting. Do not award a reduction merely because another actor ended the encounter. The original next owner-Start time supplies the outside deadline.

   **Same-epoch re-entry:** retain allowance identity, spending, activities and settlement status. Entry itself settles nothing. If a genuine, still-upcoming regular End occurs in initiative, settle the pending opportunity there using the activities already attributable to it. If the End already passed, do not fabricate another. Preserve existing own-turn admission.

   **New-epoch admission:** retain the originating allowance identity and link it explicitly to the admission’s carried interval. Record the new epoch as the current context, without treating `LocalStart = -1` as an actual Start.

   For an outstanding outside interval, retain its captured deadline. Resolve it at the earlier of:

   - That captured deadline.
   - The first actual new owner Start that replaces the carried allowance.

   I propose this explicit partial-interval disposition:

   - A genuinely shortened outside interval earns **no automatic idle reduction**.
   - A paid Grounding Action retains its one PB settlement if no disqualifying magical activity occurred.
   - Magical activity prevents either reduction.
   - A previously consumed opportunity produces neither again.

   Thus a paid Action’s pending benefit is preserved, while an early admission cannot manufacture free idle recovery.

   Example: the old outside interval is `[0,6)`, and a genuine new encounter admits at time 4:

   | First actual new owner Start | Old interval treatment |
   |---|---|
   | 4 | Close as partial before that Start; no free idle reduction; settle eligible paid Grounding once |
   | 6 | Complete at its original deadline, then process the new Start |
   | 8 | Complete once at time 6; retain the carried allowance until the real Start at 8 |

   In the last case, time 6 is **only the previously captured accounting deadline**. It is not an old-calendar Action refresh, recharge tick or invented new-calendar turn. Do not continue producing old-calendar accounting intervals afterward.

   Admission can coincide with an actual index-zero Start. Record those as distinct ordered events: admission itself grants nothing; the genuine Start performs its existing refresh.

   Existing skipped-Start behavior, including successful retreat, must remain explicit. Deriving `LatestStart` from time alone is insufficient proof that a refresh actually occurred.

   Two current integration points require versioned changes:

   - `PostRecoveryOldEndsSettled`.
   - `FerryOldEndsSettled`, with their restoration validators.

   They currently require old casting-End records. The successor must instead prove the correct completed or carried accounting disposition. Keep their physical contact, source, closure, controller and initiative requirements; **do not satisfy them by manufacturing an End**.

4. **CAL-04 — Insert accounting into the existing event order**

   Preserve regular initiative Starts/Ends and captured effect endpoints. The amendment should specify these ordering constraints explicitly:

   1. Credit actual elapsed movement and compatible work through the endpoint using the existing interval rules.
   2. Resolve genuine outgoing regular-End events in their established source order. Tactical Dissonance settlement remains End maintenance, before end-ending effects expire.
   3. Complete any outside accounting interval due at this endpoint, before the incoming allowance can be used. A tactical settlement already consumed for that identity prevents another settlement.
   4. Apply start-ending/absolute expirations before tied recharge and voluntary admission. In particular, an expired Consecrate zone cannot be relabeled as a replacement.
   5. Process actual owner Starts once: existing refresh/recharge, permitted recovery, death saves and other source-ordered Start effects. Open the new allowance’s accounting identity once.
   6. Preserve each existing work-completion and pending-choice procedure’s established priority. A mandatory choice stops continuation at its actual phase; resumption must not repeat earlier settlement or refresh.
   7. Complete lawful closure/admission processing and permit voluntary input only when mandatory boundary work is resolved.

   This is not permission to reorder unrelated job or life procedures. The written contract must bind these insertion points to the actual dispatcher and its continuation state.

   Sparse advancement may collapse only equivalent empty intervals. It must retain an explicit settlement watermark or reviewed range representation, distinguish completed zero-effect intervals from open ones, and preserve every meaningful activity, transition and receipt. No unreviewed history compaction.

   One evidence clarification is necessary: one large advance and several smaller advance commands naturally have different receipts and revisions. Compare their **canonical gameplay-state projection and ordered mechanical events**, retaining both real command histories. Do not claim their raw full saves are byte-identical. The five paths using the same logical command sequence still require their defined canonical equality.

5. **CAL-05 — Shared admission, distinct source consumers and strict causal records**

   Use one authoritative context assessment for the six operations, returning the actual allowance identity, activity segment, settlement status, current epoch and any carry provenance. Preserve each operation’s own source checks.

   | Consumer | Required integration |
   |---|---|
   | `UseConsecrate` | Record late magical activity; pay Action/2RP; preserve fixed geometry, original expiry and separate recharge |
   | `UseHealingRite` | Record one magical producer; preserve actual dice/payment and base Rite → Ground → Radiance → Aura order |
   | `UseDivineInvocation` | Preserve earned Bishop/selected mode, Action/3RP/2Conviction, actual healing/cure producer, vent and recharge |
   | `CastKnownSpell` | Preserve known-source access, components/custody, concentration, targets, exact RNG, Dissonance and Refrain |
   | `FocusDetectedAura` | Record magical focus activity with its Action; preserve actual aura visibility/protection; no second casting cost |
   | `GroundCastingStrain` | Record nonmagical paid Grounding against an unconsumed settlement opportunity |

   Separate the calendar part of `RadianceRules.OwnTurnFailure` from Radiance ownership. Shared late-action admission must not accidentally require that passive, and moving the calendar check must not bypass its genuine acquisition gate.

   Keep downstream cadence identities distinct:

   - Radiance uses its existing once-per-own-interval entitlement, keyed through the carried allowance identity.
   - Ground remains once per actual recipient/Rite pulse, not once per calendar segment.
   - Aura remains tied to the actual qualifying healing/save event.
   - Protected vent requires actual qualifying Conviction expenditure and its own cadence token.
   - Invocation’s direct Radiance mode does not become a Healing Rite or acquire Ground/passive-Radiance/Aura triggers merely because both heal.

   **Recharge remains separate from activity settlement.** Preserve the accepted actual-owner-Start cadence and skipped-Start handling. For example, under the retained Consecration cadence, an outside use at `s+3` has expiry `s+21`, while three subsequent owner Starts may complete recharge at `s+18`. The new accounting rule must not move either endpoint. Explicitly identify this as the retained approved calendar binding, rather than silently presenting it as a newly derived application-relative timer.

   A use before the first new-epoch owner Start needs a versioned recharge record that can represent the genuine carried origin and “no new Start processed yet.” Never call `epoch.Start(-1)` or manufacture a new local Start to fill the old record shape.

   The minimum causal data is:

   | Record responsibility | Required facts |
   |---|---|
   | Allowance lineage | Actual origin/refresh event, actor, carried predecessor and admission links |
   | Activity segment | Actual mode/epoch, opening and closing events, allowance identity |
   | Activity | Actual command, time, source-qualified classification, payment/result links and segment |
   | Settlement | Covered interval/activities, completion reason, eligibility, PB, Dissonance before/after and actual cause |
   | Transition | Old/new context, unchanged carried spending/cadence, pending or completed settlement disposition |
   | Cadence/recharge | Actual producer and consumed entitlement; actual processed Start cursor, including carry/skip semantics |

   Existing names or representations may differ; these facts cannot be inferred from caller flags.

   Audit every validator using the old `SpellTurnIdentity` or short-slot assumption, including downstream consumers and Sanctuary interval caching. Do not globally relax `ValidTurn` and thereby weaken unrelated authority or retry checks.

For the prospective evidence plan, I recommend separate genuine branches from fresh successor genesis:

- **Main connected branch:** replay the lawful accepted acquisition/funding route, reach post-recovery closure and owned Bishop/Consecrate, create the zone at `s+3`, then demonstrate genuine Ground healing or the Ferry attack contribution, real admission and paid continuation.
- **Strain branch:** build nonzero Dissonance through actual admitted repeated spells, then demonstrate late magical suppression, idle and paid Grounding in separately retained branches.
- **Closure branch:** close after a real idle tactical End with an unspent Action; prove that late activation preserves that End and produces no second reduction.
- **Transition branches:** carry both pending and already-settled accounting, including before-first-Start and legitimate same-epoch re-entry where the existing route admits it.
- **Consumer branches:** genuine late Rite, Invocation, spell and Detect-focus uses with their actual ownership, resources and targets. Do not require one campaign to fund mutually exclusive demonstrations.

Save/restore must cover pending accounting, completed-End remainders, late use, transition carry and resumed mandatory decisions. Forgeries must fail for relabeled segments, reopened zero-effect settlements, fabricated refreshes, removed magical activity, changed deadlines, duplicated vent/rider uses and substituted paid producers—even with recomputed checksums.

Keep profiles through115 on their exact prior semantics and serialization. Use a fresh opt-in successor profile after checking availability. Existing TAC-10/Consecration allocations remain closed within their scopes; a newly blocked successor witness would need its own explicit disposition.

I inspected the accepted definition/verdict, pinned source and policies, and current settlement, entry, closure, healing, recharge and validation code. All **25 published binding blobs matched their recorded lengths and SHA-256 values**, and the local engine tree matched `6cce215d2ce46bebcfd15f69f61dc324545c23d7`. I made no edits and ran no builds, gameplay, tests or qualification.

**CAL-01–05 remain proposed pending the exact contract and Codex concurrence.** The two policy choices that must be stated plainly in that contract are the consumed-settlement Grounding restriction and the shortened-interval treatment; neither should become implementation behavior by implication.

codexInitialDisposition: The separated allowance-lineage/activity-segment/settlement design addresses the audited source conflict while retaining tactical End semantics. Prepare an exact contract including the explicit consumed-settlement Grounding restriction, shortened interval disposition, concrete scheduler hooks, causal codec changes and all six consumers. Actual source/API acceptance remains open.
